raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: Broncholithiasis is characterized by a calcified lymph node eroding into the bronchial lumen, causing obstruction and subsequent segmental atelectasis or post-obstructive pneumonia; the images show left lower lobe consolidation/atelectasis consistent with this mechanism, distinguishing it from simple calcified granulomas (D) or non-calcified masses (B).
